pdf_note: rasterised independently by the verifier at 300 dpi

x_axis.note: slope axis of the source plot, which is VERTICAL: pixel ROWS of the grey dashed gridlines at 0 and 40 deg (86.6 px per 10 deg)

y_axis.note: slip axis of the source plot, which is HORIZONTAL: pixel COLUMNS of the grey dashed gridlines at slip 0 and 0.8

marker.identification: manual: black filled circles (MGRU3 2022 SLOPElab Tests, GRC1); found as blobs that survive a 15 px disc opening of the black mask (lines and stars removed), bounding box centres; the two lowest circles touch a triangle and were centred from their unobstructed left edge and the circle diameter of 21 px
marker.swap_note: the source plot has slip on x and slope on y; every point px is given as [row, column] so that the output x is slope and the output y is slip; do not use colour refinement with this ordering

meta.source_title: A study demonstrating that using gravitational offset to prepare extraterrestrial mobility missions is misleading (Hu, Li, Rogg, Schepelmann, Chandler, Kamrin, Negrut; Journal of Field Robotics, 2025; author manuscript in NASA NTRS 20250001809)
meta.vehicle: MGRU3 (Moon Gravitation Representative Unit 3) VIPER test rover, four wheels, on the SLOPE lab tilt bed
meta.comparability_note: Series 'MGRU3 2022 SLOPElab Tests, GRC1' (black circles, dotted line), not the 2021 series (left pointing triangles, dash dot line). Seven points. Output x (slope) comes from the vertical axis.
